Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Vendor privacy & residency questions — Redwood platform

Hi Rohan,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers and the ability to pin model versions. Before we go further on procurement, our internal privacy and finance teams asked for a few concrete answers so we can map to our vendor approval checklist: 

- Can Redwood sign a FERPA addendum for student data? Any specific exclusions?
- For GLBA-covered workflows (student financial aid servicing handled by our partner bank), do you offer a GLBA/GLBA-like addendum and what residency options apply?
- For HIPAA/BAA: we may route some health-related counseling transcripts through the platform; do you support a BAA and is on-prem deployment required?
- Subprocessor list and geography: we need a current list of subprocessors and whether any subprocessors process data outside the US.
- KMS options: is customer-managed KMS available for hosted or Dedicated?

I've attached our RFP extract (Summit_Academy_RFP_2027.pdf) with the vendor checklist for reference. Can you respond to the questions above and share any standard addenda we can review? If needed, we can set up a short call with procurement + legal next week.

Appreciate it,

Maya Singh
Head of Partnerships
Summit Academy

[attachment: Summit_Academy_RFP_2027.pdf]

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan_mehta@redwood.ai>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@summitacademy.org>, Legal <legal@summitacademy.org>, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Vendor privacy & residency questions — Redwood platform

Maya — thanks for the clear list and the RFP excerpt. High level answers below; happy to follow up with legal/solutions for details.

1) FERPA: Yes, we execute a FERPA addendum for K12 and higher-ed customers processing student education records. Standard exclusions: aggregated/anonymized analytics and provider-submitted metadata (we can discuss precise language).

2) GLBA: We have a GLBA-friendly addendum tailored for financial-data workflows. For GLBA-covered processing, we recommend either Dedicated or Private deployments (VPC/on-prem) to provide stronger isolation and contractual controls. Hosted can be considered with residency and subprocessor assurances but will require specific routing and contractual language.

3) HIPAA / BAA: We will sign a BAA. For high-volume PHI use cases we typically recommend Private (customer-managed) or Dedicated with strict KMS controls and audit logging to meet client auditor expectations.

4) Subprocessors: We maintain a published subprocessor roster. Short answer: primary infra subprocessors (cloud hosting, CDN) may be in the US and EU depending on region. We can provide a current CSV and highlight any non-US processing by data type.

5) KMS: Customer-managed KMS is available for Dedicated and Private; for hosted customers we offer multi-tenant KMS with customer key-wrapping (BYOK) and HSM-backed options for enterprise contracts.

Attachments: I'm including our standard DPA template and a short SOC 2 high-level summary for a first pass.

Next steps: can I introduce you to Neha (our privacy counsel) and Laura (solutions lead) to walk through the RFP checklist? If so, propose 30 minutes on Tue/Wed next week.

Cheers,

Rohan Mehta
Senior Account Executive, Regulated Verticals
Redwood Inference

[attachments: Redwood_DPA_Template_v3.docx, SOC2-Report-HighLevel-summary.pdf]

Rohan & team — quick legal summary and recommended language to keep the engagement moving: 

- FERPA: We will sign a FERPA addendum. Proposed non-negotiable items: 1) Redwood will act only on documented instructions from Summit Academy for education records; 2) logging and deletion timeline for student records aligned to contract (default: 90 days after termination unless otherwise scoped). Suggest offering a short appendix for research-use exemptions.

- GLBA: Offer a GLBA addendum that mirrors obligations in our existing GLBA templates (customer obligations + Redwood commitments). Important to call out: dedicated environment requirement for GLBA "covered processing" OR strict isolation + customer-managed KMS for hosted if Summit cannot accept Dedicated.

- BAA: We will sign a BAA for covered PHI; requirement: audit logging and exportable access logs; for high-volume PHI recommend Private deployment.

- Subprocessors & Transfers: Provide an up-to-date subprocessor CSV and a statement that no new cross-border subprocessors will be added for Summit-covered data types without 30 days' notice. For EU/UK transfer questions we will reference our standard SCCs and data transfer impact assessment.

Suggested redline bullets for initial DPA: residency commitments (US-only by data class), max subprocessors list and notification clause, KMS key ownership & rotation rules, and audit access for SOC2 reports.

I attached a short checklist and a proposed one-page addendum summary you can share ahead of the call. Happy to join the meeting; my availability Tue 10:00-11:00 PT and Wed 14:00-16:00 PT.

Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel
Redwood Inference
